correctness.rationale: For uniform SI source and any two monitored vertices on P_n, infection reaches each directional nearest sentinel via sums of independent unit exponential edge waiting times. Their independence gives the Erlang-product survival law. Exhausting the ten P5 pairs into six reflection orbits yields exact displayed survival polynomials, and signs of differences reduce the global optimization to three pairs. Calculus gives exactly two unique positive crossing roots with xi<eta. Direct comparison on P2,P3,P4 proves sharpness. A separate first-event Markov recurrence has been executed from the local checker and matched all 20 two-sentinel pairs at four rational Laplace values (80 exact fraction equalities) and the exact mean-class tables. The finite program checks the formulas but the continuum uniqueness depends on the analytic derivative proof, not enumeration.

originality.rationale: Compared the exact two-objective claim with the known four-site SI path deadline law, semantic literature queries targeting sensor/path/first detection and relevant research literature. The four-site computation shows a four-site deadline switch and generic early/late behavior but not the five-site strict mean-vs-deadline separation or three-regime classification. General submodular outbreak detection and minimum-delay methods do not logically imply a symbolic sharp lower bound on this different cross-objective property. The 2015 mobile-networks full text remains inaccessible, so historical priority is qualified.

value.rationale: Early-warning systems must trade probability of detection before a fixed intervention deadline against average detection delay. The small path provides the sharp first structurally nontrivial case where these objectives provably conflict, with three qualitatively distinct exact time regimes and an endpoint solution whose mean detection delay is 20% worse than the minimum. Unlike a merely renamed finite enumeration, the result pinpoints the precise existence threshold and continuous-time decision boundaries using first-passage structure. No empirical applicability or general graph-family theorem is claimed.
